title: Unconditional AsRawFd import breaks the macOS CI leg under -D warnings
description:
persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:2 has 'use std::os::unix::io::AsRawFd;' at module scope with no cfg gate. Its only consumer is stream.as_raw_fd() at line 17, inside '#[cfg(target_os = "linux")] fn attest_peer'. Line 49's std::os::unix::io::RawFd is fully qualified and needs no import.

On macOS the import is therefore unused -> unused_imports -> under CI's '-D warnings' it is a hard error, failing the check (macos-latest) leg.

Everything else in the file IS correctly gated (SO_PEERCRED, libc::ucred, getsockopt, the libc::getuid unsafe block, hash_file), and the /run/user paths elsewhere are runtime strings that compile fine on macOS. This single line is the whole macOS compile break.

Fix: '#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]' on the import, or move it inside attest_peer.

Currently masked: the macOS leg dies earlier at protoc (.11), so this only becomes visible once that is fixed. Not machine-verified — no macOS toolchain available locally; established by source analysis, agreed by two independent agents.
